requirements.quote:
While name server implementations are free to use any internal data
structures they choose, the suggested structure consists of three major
parts:

   - A "catalog" data structure which lists the zones available to
     this server, and a "pointer" to the zone data structure.  The
     main purpose of this structure is to find the nearest ancestor
     zone, if any, for arriving standard queries.
requirements.condition: When following the suggested three-part database design.
requirements.required_behavior: The suggested catalog lists the zones available to the server.
requirements.why_checkable: The catalog entries can be compared with the zones held by the server.

requirements.quote:
All of these data structures can be implemented an identical tree
structure format, with different data chained off the nodes in different
parts: in the catalog the data is pointers to zones, while in the zone
and cache data structures, the data will be RRs.
requirements.condition: When choosing the optional identical-tree representation for catalog, zone, and cache structures.
requirements.required_behavior: Attach zone pointers as the catalog tree node data.
requirements.why_checkable: The data associated with catalog tree nodes can be inspected.

requirements.condition: When query processing traverses a database tree.
requirements.required_behavior: Use case-insensitive label comparisons during traversal.
requirements.why_checkable: Tree lookups using names that differ only in letter case can exercise label comparison.

requirements.quote:
One way to solve the case problem is to store the labels for each node
in two pieces: a standardized-case representation of the label where all
ASCII characters are in a single case, together with a bit mask that
denotes which characters are actually of a different case.
requirements.condition: When choosing the suggested two-piece representation of labels.
requirements.required_behavior: Store a standardized-case label representation in which all ASCII characters use a single case.
requirements.why_checkable: The optional normalized-label representation can be inspected for consistent ASCII casing.

requirements.quote:
The
branching factor diversity can be handled using a simple linked list for
a node until the branching factor exceeds some threshold, and
transitioning to a hash structure after the threshold is exceeded.
requirements.condition: When choosing the suggested linked-list-to-hash strategy for branching-factor diversity and a node has not exceeded the selected branching threshold.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a simple linked list for that node under this optional strategy.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected threshold and node representation can be checked on either side of the boundary.

requirements.quote:
The
branching factor diversity can be handled using a simple linked list for
a node until the branching factor exceeds some threshold, and
transitioning to a hash structure after the threshold is exceeded.
requirements.condition: When choosing the suggested linked-list-to-hash strategy and a node exceeds the selected branching threshold.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition that node to a hash structure under this optional strategy.
requirements.why_checkable: Increasing a node beyond the selected threshold can exercise the representation transition.

requirements.quote:
In designing the tree
framework the designer should recognize that query processing will need
to traverse the tree using case-insensitive label comparisons; and that



Mockapetris                                                    [Page 37]


RFC 1035        Domain Implementation and Specification    November 1987


in real data, a few nodes have a very high branching factor (100-1000 or
more), but the vast majority have a very low branching factor (0-1).

One way to solve the case problem is to store the labels for each node
in two pieces: a standardized-case representation of the label where all
ASCII characters are in a single case, together with a bit mask that
denotes which characters are actually of a different case.  The
branching factor diversity can be handled using a simple linked list for
a node until the branching factor exceeds some threshold, and
transitioning to a hash structure after the threshold is exceeded.  In
any case, hash structures used to store tree sections must insure that
hash functions and procedures preserve the casing conventions of the
DNS.
requirements.condition: When hash structures store sections of the database tree.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure hash functions and procedures preserve the case-insensitive label comparisons required for query traversal.
requirements.why_checkable: Names differing only in case can be checked for equivalent lookup through hashed tree sections.

requirements.quote:
- The catalog structure can be an almost static structure that
     need change only when the system administrator changes the
     zones supported by the server.
requirements.condition: When implementing the catalog data structure.
requirements.required_behavior: The catalog may remain almost static and need change only when the administrator changes the zones supported by the server.
requirements.why_checkable: Catalog update triggers can be inspected to determine whether the implementation adopts this permitted static-catalog design.

requirements.quote:
This structure can also be
     used to store parameters used to control refreshing
     activities.
requirements.condition: When implementing the catalog data structure.
requirements.required_behavior: The catalog may store parameters controlling zone refreshing activities.
requirements.why_checkable: Refresh-control parameter storage can be inspected as an optional catalog capability.

requirements.quote:
- The individual data structures for zones allow a zone to be
     replaced simply by changing a pointer in the catalog.  Zone
     refresh operations can build a new structure and, when
     complete, splice it into the database via a simple pointer
     replacement.
requirements.condition: When adopting the suggested zone-refresh method that builds a replacement zone structure.
requirements.required_behavior: Complete the new zone structure before splicing it into the database by replacing the catalog pointer.
requirements.why_checkable: The publication point for a replacement structure can be checked against completion of its construction.

requirements.quote:
It is very important that when a zone is
     refreshed, queries should not use old and new data
     simultaneously.
requirements.condition: When a zone is refreshed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Queries should not use old and new zone data simultaneously.
requirements.why_checkable: Concurrent queries during a refresh can be checked for mixed-version zone data.

requirements.quote:
- With the proper search procedures, authoritative data in zones
     will always "hide", and hence take precedence over, cached
     data.
requirements.condition: When authoritative zone data and cached data compete during database searching.
requirements.required_behavior: Give authoritative zone data precedence over cached data.
requirements.why_checkable: A lookup with conflicting authoritative and cached records can verify which source takes precedence.

requirements.quote:
The use of separate structures for the different parts of the database
is motivated by several factors:

   - The catalog structure can be an almost static structure that
     need change only when the system administrator changes the
     zones supported by the server.  This structure can also be
     used to store parameters used to control refreshing
     activities.

   - The individual data structures for zones allow a zone to be
     replaced simply by changing a pointer in the catalog.  Zone
     refresh operations can build a new structure and, when
     complete, splice it into the database via a simple pointer
     replacement.  It is very important that when a zone is
     refreshed, queries should not use old and new data
     simultaneously.

   - With the proper search procedures, authoritative data in zones
     will always "hide", and hence take precedence over, cached
     data.

   - Errors in zone definitions that cause overlapping zones, etc.,
     may cause erroneous responses to queries, but problem
     determination is simplified, and the contents of one "bad"
     zone can't corrupt another.
requirements.condition: When using the suggested separate structures for individual zones and a zone contains erroneous definitions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow the contents of one erroneous zone to corrupt another zone.
requirements.why_checkable: Storage isolation can be inspected and erroneous overlapping zone definitions can be checked for changes to another zone.

requirements.quote:
The use of separate structures for the different parts of the database
is motivated by several factors:

   - The catalog structure can be an almost static structure that
     need change only when the system administrator changes the
     zones supported by the server.  This structure can also be
     used to store parameters used to control refreshing
     activities.

   - The individual data structures for zones allow a zone to be
     replaced simply by changing a pointer in the catalog.  Zone
     refresh operations can build a new structure and, when
     complete, splice it into the database via a simple pointer
     replacement.  It is very important that when a zone is
     refreshed, queries should not use old and new data
     simultaneously.

   - With the proper search procedures, authoritative data in zones
     will always "hide", and hence take precedence over, cached
     data.

   - Errors in zone definitions that cause overlapping zones, etc.,
     may cause erroneous responses to queries, but problem
     determination is simplified, and the contents of one "bad"
     zone can't corrupt another.

   - Since the cache is most frequently updated, it is most
     vulnerable to corruption during system restarts.  It can also
     become full of expired RR data.  In either case, it can easily
     be discarded without disturbing zone data.
requirements.condition: When using separate database structures and the cache is corrupted during a system restart or full of expired resource records.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the cache to be discarded without disturbing zone data.
requirements.why_checkable: Discarding the cache under either stated condition can be checked for preservation of zone data.
